newsitem.title: USA: Bradley County, Tenn., rejects wheel tax.
newsitem.headline: Bradley County, Tenn., rejects wheel tax.

text.p: Voters in Tennessee's Bradley County narrowly defeated a proposal to levy a $20 tax on cars to fund school programs, elections officials said Wednesday.
The proposal failed 4,872 to 4,173 in Tuesday's referendum.
The county commissiom approved the wheel tax and a property tax increase earlier this year to raise $40 million to meet state mandates in the Basic Education Program.

The original proposal drew little criticism but when commissioners amended it to include leased vehicles and motorcycles, unhappy residents collected enough petition signatures to force the referendum.
Fifty Tennessee counties levy wheel taxes ranging from $10 to $73.50 while seven municipalities levy a similar city sticker tax.
